  docs_ownership: |
    library-releaser owns documentation tasks: TypeDoc configuration, doc generation, docs scripts.
    When docs need updating or generating for a release, delegate to library-releaser.
    library-validator no longer handles documentation — only testing and quality gates.
  api_change_policy: |
    MANDATORY: Any change to CLI command behavior or to the API of public functions must be
    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.
    ENFORCEMENT: Every /issue chain that touches CLI or public API MUST include a library-releaser
    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.

  docs_awareness: |
    All agents have read access to docs/markdown/ (8 files: overview, getting-started, authentication,
    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.

    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.

    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."

    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:

Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."

    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."

Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

# Getting started

This guide walks you through installing agentrack and running through a complete first session. By the end, you'll know how to create, update, and inspect issues using both the CLI and the JavaScript API.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js >= 20** -- Agentrack uses modern JavaScript features and requires Node 20 or later.
- **Git** -- Your project must be a git repository. Agentrack stores issue data on a dedicated branch.

## Installation

Install agentrack as a dependency in your project:

```bash
npm install agentrack
```

This gives you access to the JavaScript API (`import { Tracker } from "agentrack"`) and the CLI command.

### Using the CLI

After installation, the `agt` command is available via:

```bash
npx agt <command>
```

For frequent use, link it globally:

```bash
npm link
# Now you can use "agt" directly
agt <command>
```

## Your first session (CLI)

### 1. Initialize the tracker

Run `init` in your git repository to create the `.agentrack` directory and set up the storage branch:

```bash
agt init
```

Output:

```json
{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/your/project" }
```

This creates the `.agentrack/` directory (which lives on a separate git branch) with the index file, config, and user registry. See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md) for details on how this works.

### 2. Create an issue

```bash
agt create "Investigate slow database queries" \
  --description "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load. Start by profiling the database queries." \
  --status todo \
  --assignee "alice" \
  --tags "performance,backend" \
  --priority 2
```

Output:

```json
{ "id": "m1x2k9ab" }
```

The issue ID is a short, time-sortable string. Save it -- you'll use it to reference the issue.

### 3. List your issues

```bash
agt list
```

Output:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "m1x2k9ab",
    "title": "Investigate slow database queries",
    "status": "todo",
    "assignee": "alice",
    "tags": ["performance", "backend"],
    "parentId": null,
    "priority": 2
  }
]
```

You can filter by status, assignee, tags, or parent. For example, `agt list --status open --assignee alice` shows all open issues assigned to alice.

### 4. View an issue's full details

```bash
agt view m1x2k9ab
```

Output:

```json
{
  "id": "m1x2k9ab",
  "title": "Investigate slow database queries",
  "description": "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load...",
  "status": "todo",
  "assignee": "alice",
  "tags": ["performance", "backend"],
  "parentId": null,
  "priority": 2,
  "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
  "createdBy": "anonymous",
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z"
}
```

### 5. Update the issue

Move the issue to in-progress:

```bash
agt update m1x2k9ab --status "in-progress"
```

Output:

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

You can update any combination of fields in a single command:

```bash
agt update m1x2k9ab --status "done" --description "Found and fixed the N+1 query in the dashboard endpoint."
```

### 6. View the event history

Every change is recorded as an immutable event. View the full history:

```bash
agt history m1x2k9ab
```

Output:

```json
[
  { "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z", "type": "creation", "author": "anonymous" },
  {
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
    "type": "update",
    "author": "anonymous",
    "content": {
      "title": "Investigate slow database queries",
      "description": "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load...",
      "status": "todo",
      "assignee": "alice",
      "tags": ["performance", "backend"],
      "priority": 2
    }
  },
  {
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T11:00:00.000Z",
    "type": "update",
    "author": "anonymous",
    "content": { "status": "in-progress" }
  }
]
```

The history is the source of truth. The `view` command computes the current state by replaying these events.

## Your first session (JavaScript)

The same workflow using the JavaScript API:

```javascript
import { Tracker } from "agentrack";

const tracker = new Tracker(); // resolves .agentrack/ from cwd

// 1. Initialize
await tracker.init();

// 2. Create an issue
const { id } = await tracker.create({
  title: "Investigate slow database queries",
  description: "Users report the dashboard takes 10+ seconds to load...",
  status: "todo",
  assignee: "alice",
  tags: ["performance", "backend"],
  priority: 2,
});
console.log("Created issue:", id);

// 3. List issues
const issues = await tracker.list({ status: "open" });
console.log("Open issues:", issues);

// 4. View an issue
const issue = await tracker.view(id);
console.log("Issue details:", issue);

// 5. Update the issue
await tracker.update(id, { status: "in-progress" });

// 6. View history
const events = await tracker.history(id);
console.log("Event log:", events);
```

The `Tracker` constructor optionally accepts a `cwd` argument if you need to target a specific project directory:

```javascript
const tracker = new Tracker("/path/to/project");
```

## Where to go next

- [Authentication](./authentication.md) -- Set up users and tokens so multiple agents can attribute their work
- [The issue object](./issue-object.md) -- Understand issue properties, statuses, and the event sourcing model
- [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md) -- Organize issues into epics and track dependencies
- [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md) -- Full command documentation with all flags and examples
- [JavaScript reference](./javascript-reference.md) -- Complete API reference for the Tracker class

1	# Configurable Branch Name for `agt init`
2	
3	**Status: REVIEWED — Updated 2026-05-21 to incorporate review feedback from mpe3pvr2yu and mpe3pv74lo**
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	Add a `--branch <name>` flag to the `agt init` subcommand, allowing users to specify which orphan branch stores the agentrack data. The default remains `_agentrack`. This enables multiple agentrack instances per repository (each on its own branch), and allows the library's own test suite to initialize a dedicated test branch rather than colliding with the project's real `_agentrack` data.
8	
9	## Requirements
10	
11	### AC1: `--branch` flag on `agt init`
12	
13	`agt init` accepts an optional `--branch <name>` flag. When provided, the specified branch name is used instead of `_agentrack` for all worktree operations (orphan branch creation, worktree mount, push, pull).
14	
15	When omitted, the behavior is identical to today: branch name is `_agentrack`.
16	
17	```
18	agt init                    # branch: _agentrack,  dir: .agentrack/
19	agt init --branch testing   # branch: _testing,    dir: .testing/
20	agt init --branch _ci       # branch: _ci,         dir: .ci/
21	agt init --branch myproject # branch: _myproject,  dir: .myproject/
22	```
23	
24	**Normalization rules:**
25	
26	1. Strip leading underscores from user input
27	2. Prepend `_` for branch name, `.` for directory name
28	3. This means `--branch testing` and `--branch _testing` produce the same result
29	4. Default (no flag): branch `_agentrack`, directory `.agentrack/`
30	
31	| Flag value | Branch name | Directory name |
32	|------------|-------------|----------------|
33	| (none)     | `_agentrack` | `.agentrack/` |
34	| `testing`  | `_testing`   | `.testing/` |
35	| `_ci`      | `_ci`        | `.ci/` |
36	| `myproject`| `_myproject` | `.myproject/` |
37	
38	Each branch/directory pair is independent, allowing multiple agentrack instances per repository (each mounted at its own path).
39	
40	### AC2: Branch name stored in config + pointer file
41	
42	After `agt init`, the chosen branch name is recorded in two places:
43	
44	**1. Inside the worktree config** — `config.json` in the worktree directory:
45	
46	```json
47	{
48	  "version": 1,
49	  "auth": { "mode": "open" },
50	  "branch": "_testing"
51	}
52	```
53	
54	**2. As a pointer file in the main repo root** — `.agentrack.json` at the repo root (NOT inside the worktree):
55	
56	```json
57	{
58	  "branch": "_testing"
59	}
60	```
61	
62	This pointer file solves the circular discovery problem: to find the config, you need to know the directory, but the directory comes from the config. The pointer file at a fixed, well-known location (`cwd/.agentrack.json`) breaks the cycle.
63	
64	- The pointer file is created during `agt init` and must be committed to the main branch (not the worktree branch).
65	- During `push`/`pull` and all other commands, read `.agentrack.json` to discover which worktree directory to use.
66	- For backward compatibility: if `.agentrack.json` does not exist, assume branch `_agentrack` and directory `.agentrack/`.
67	- The existing default init continues to produce `config.json` without a `branch` field (backward compatible — code falls back to `_agentrack` when absent).
68	- The pointer file is always named `.agentrack.json` regardless of the branch name.
69	
70	### AC3: `push` and `pull` respect the configured branch
71	
72	`agt push` and `agt pull` read the branch name from the pointer file (`cwd/.agentrack.json`) and operate on that branch's worktree. They derive the correct directory (`.agentrack/` vs `.testing/` etc.) from the pointer file's `branch` field. If the pointer file is absent, fall back to `_agentrack` / `.agentrack/`.
73	
74	### AC4: Worktree module reads branch from pointer file
75	
76	The `worktree.ts` module currently hardcodes `WORKTREE_BRANCH = '_agentrack'` and `WORKTREE_DIR = '.agentrack'`. These become derived from the pointer file:
77	
78	```typescript
79	// Before
80	export const WORKTREE_BRANCH = '_agentrack';
81	export const WORKTREE_DIR = '.agentrack';
82	
83	// After: resolved from pointer file or defaults
84	export const DEFAULT_BRANCH = '_agentrack';
85	export const DEFAULT_DIR = '.agentrack';
86	
87	export function normalizeBranchName(input: string): { branch: string; dir: string }
88	// Strips leading underscores, prepends _ and . respectively
89	// IMPORTANT: Rejects slashes — see AC8
90	
91	export function resolveWorktreePaths(cwd: string): { branch: string; dir: string }
92	// Reads .agentrack.json from cwd to determine active branch/dir
93	// Falls back to DEFAULT_BRANCH/DEFAULT_DIR if pointer file absent
94	```
95	
96	**Important:** During `init`, there's a chicken-and-egg problem — the pointer file doesn't exist yet, so we can't read the branch from it. The `--branch` flag value must be passed through to the worktree init functions explicitly. After init completes, the pointer file is written.
97	
98	### AC5: `isWorktreeInitialized` and `resolveTrackerDir` must discover the active instance
99	
100	The current check looks for `.agentrack/` specifically. `resolution.ts` has `const AGENTACK_DIR = ".agentrack"` used by `resolveTrackerDir()` which walks up the filesystem. Both must be generalized:
101	
102	- **During `init`:** The command already knows the target directory from the `--branch` flag (or default). Check that specific directory.
103	- **During all other commands:** Read the pointer file (`.agentrack.json`) to discover the branch, derive the directory, then check that path.
104	- **`resolveTrackerDir()`** must read the pointer file at each level during its walk-up to determine the correct directory name. If no pointer file is found, fall back to `.agentrack/`.
105	
106	Similarly, `tracker.ts` has `const AGENTACK_DIR = ".agentrack"` for the non-git fallback path. This must also be derived from the pointer file or passed as a parameter.
107	
108	Do NOT scan for all agentrack directories — just resolve the single active one from the pointer file.
109	
110	### AC6: Error cases for `--branch`
111	
112	| Condition | Error code | Message |
113	|-----------|-----------|---------|
114	| Branch name contains spaces or invalid git chars | `INVALID_BRANCH_NAME` | "Branch name '<name>' is not a valid git branch name" |
115	| Branch name is empty | `INVALID_BRANCH_NAME` | "Branch name cannot be empty" |
116	| Branch name contains slashes | `INVALID_BRANCH_NAME` | "Branch name cannot contain slashes (slashes would create nested directories)" |
117	| Directory already exists (for that branch) and is not a worktree | `MIGRATION_REQUIRED` | Same as current, but with the specific directory name |
118	| Branch already exists but with different content | `BRANCH_CONFLICT` | "Branch '<name>' already exists but does not contain agentrack data" |
119	
120	### AC7: Backward compatibility
121	
122	All existing behavior is preserved:
123	- `agt init` without `--branch` works exactly as before
124	- Existing repos with `_agentrack` branch and `.agentrack/` directory continue to work
125	- `config.json` files without a `branch` field are treated as `_agentrack`
126	- Repos without a `.agentrack.json` pointer file fall back to `_agentrack` / `.agentrack/`
127	- `WORKTREE_BRANCH` and `WORKTREE_DIR` exports are replaced with `DEFAULT_BRANCH` and `DEFAULT_DIR` (breaking change acceptable at 0.x)
128	
129	### AC8: No slashes in branch names
130	
131	Branch names containing `/` are explicitly rejected by the normalization function. While git supports slash-separated branch names (e.g., `feature/foo`), allowing them would create nested directories (`.feature/foo/`) which:
132	- May have non-existent parent directories
133	- Complicate git worktree operations
134	- Break the walk-up resolution in `resolution.ts`
135	
136	Users who want hierarchical naming can use dashes: `--branch feature-test` → `_feature-test` / `.feature-test/`.
137	
138	## API / Interface Changes
139	
140	### CLI changes
141	
142	```bash
143	agt init [--branch <name>]
144	```
145	
146	The `--branch` flag is optional. When provided, `<name>` is normalized per AC1.

148	### Config schema change
149	
150	`config.json` gains an optional `branch` field:
151	
152	```typescript
153	interface Config {
154	  version: number;
155	  auth: AuthConfig;
156	  branch?: string;  // NEW — defaults to '_agentrack' when absent
157	}

162	The hardcoded constants become dynamic:
163	
164	```typescript
165	// Before

167	export const WORKTREE_DIR = '.agentrack';
168	
169	// After
170	export const DEFAULT_BRANCH = '_agentrack';
171	export const DEFAULT_DIR = '.agentrack';
172

206	## Implementation Notes
207	
208	### Flag parsing
209	
210	The CLI uses `commander` (or similar). Add the option to the init subcommand:
211	
212	```typescript
213	program
214	  .command('init')
215	  .option('--branch <name>', 'branch name for agentrack data')
216	  .action(async (options) => {
217	    const branchInput = options.branch;
218	    // ... normalize and pass to worktree init
219	  });
220	```
221	
222	### Normalization implementation
223	
224	```typescript
225	export function normalizeBranchName(input: string): { branch: string; dir: string } {
226	  // Strip leading underscores
227	  const cleaned = input.replace(/^_+/, '');
228	  if (!cleaned) throw new AgentrackError('INVALID_BRANCH_NAME', 'Branch name cannot be empty', 1);
229	
230	  // Reject slashes — they create nested directories
231	  if (cleaned.includes('/')) {
232	    throw new AgentrackError('INVALID_BRANCH_NAME', 'Branch name cannot contain slashes (would create nested directories)', 1);
233	  }
234	
235	  // Validate: no spaces, no special chars that git rejects
236	  if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*$/.test(cleaned)) {
237	    throw new AgentrackError('INVALID_BRANCH_NAME', `"${input}" is not a valid branch name`, 1);
238	  }
239	
240	  return {
241	    branch: `_${cleaned}`,
242	    dir: `.${cleaned}`,
243	  };
244	}
245	```
246	
247	### Pointer file implementation
248	
249	```typescript
250	// src/core/pointer.ts
251	import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
252	import { join } from 'node:path';
253	
254	const POINTER_FILE = '.agentrack.json';
255	
256	export interface PointerFile {
257	  branch: string;
258	}
259	
260	export async function readPointerFile(cwd: string): Promise<{ branch: string; dir: string } | null> {
261	  try {
262	    const content = await readFile(join(cwd, POINTER_FILE), 'utf-8');
263	    const pointer: PointerFile = JSON.parse(content);
264	    if (!pointer.branch) return null;
265	    // Derive dir from branch: _testing → .testing
266	    const dir = '.' + pointer.branch.replace(/^_/, '');
267	    return { branch: pointer.branch, dir };
268	  } catch {
269	    return null; // File doesn't exist or is invalid — use defaults
270	  }
271	}
272	
273	export async function writePointerFile(cwd: string, branch: string): Promise<void> {
274	  const pointer: PointerFile = { branch };
275	  await writeFile(join(cwd, POINTER_FILE), JSON.stringify(pointer, null, 2) + '\n', 'utf-8');
276	}
277	
278	// Convenience: resolve with fallback to defaults
279	export async function resolveBranch(cwd: string): Promise<{ branch: string; dir: string }> {
280	  const resolved = await readPointerFile(cwd);
281	  return resolved ?? { branch: '_agentrack', dir: '.agentrack' };
282	}
283	```
284	
285	### Config write during init
286	
287	After worktree setup and `tracker.init()`, the init command must:
288	
289	1. Write the `branch` field to `config.json` inside the worktree:
290	
291	```typescript
292	// After init completes
293	const config = readConfig(worktreeDir);
294	config.branch = normalizedBranch;  // '_testing' etc.
295	writeConfig(worktreeDir, config);
296	```
297	
298	2. Write the pointer file at the repo root:
299	
300	```typescript
301	await writePointerFile(repoRoot, normalizedBranch);
302	```
303	
304	3. Auto-commit both changes: the updated config to the worktree branch, and the pointer file to the main branch.
305	
306	### Worktree function signature changes
307	
308	Current worktree functions take `cwd: string`. They need to also know which branch/dir to target:
309	
310	```typescript
311	// Option 1: Explicit params
312	export async function initFreshWorktree(cwd: string, branch: string, dir: string): Promise<WorktreeInitResult>;
313	
314	// Option 2: Options object
315	export interface WorktreeOptions { branch: string; dir: string; }
316	export async function initFreshWorktree(cwd: string, opts: WorktreeOptions): Promise<WorktreeInitResult>;
317	```
318	
319	Option 2 is cleaner and more extensible.
320	
321	### Gitignore handling
322	
323	The gitignore entry must match the actual directory. Currently hardcoded as `/.agentrack/`. Must become dynamic and support multiple entries:
324	
325	```typescript
326	function gitignoreEntry(dir: string): string {
327	  return `/${dir}/`;
328	}
329	```
330	
331	If multiple agentrack instances exist (multiple inits with different `--branch`), each directory gets its own gitignore entry. The gitignore matching logic must also be parameterized to check for the specific directory name rather than hardcoding `.agentrack`.
332	
333	### Testing strategy
334	
335	This is a key motivator for the feature. The library's test suite can now:
336	
337	1. Create a test branch (e.g., `--branch _test-${random}`) in a temp git repo
338	2. Run full integration tests against it
339	3. Clean up by removing the worktree and branch
340	
341	This avoids tests interfering with the project's real agentrack data.
342	
343	## Out of scope
344	
345	- **Multiple simultaneous instances** — while the feature enables this, the init command doesn't check for or manage multiple instances. Each `agt init` targets one branch/directory.
346	- **Switching between instances** — no `agt switch` or similar. User manages worktrees manually via git.
347	- **Remote name configuration** — still assumes `origin`.
348	- **Migration from default to custom branch** — no tooling to move data from `_agentrack` to a custom branch.
349	- **GUI/interactive selection of branches** — flag-only, no interactive prompts.
350

32	## `agt init`
33	
34	Initialize the agentrack tracker in the current directory. Creates the `.agentrack/` directory on the `_agentrack` orphan branch.
35	
36	```bash
37	agt init
38	```
39	
40	**Output:**
41	
42	```json
43	{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
44	```
45	
46	If already initialized:
47	
48	```json
49	{ "result": "ALREADY_INITIALIZED", "path": "/path/to/project" }
50	```
51	
52	**Notes:**
53	- Must be run inside a git repository.
54	- Idempotent -- running it again won't overwrite existing data.
55	- Handles two scenarios: creates a new orphan branch (fresh) or fetches an existing one (join). See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).

492	- Cycle detection runs for each blocker. If any would create a cycle, the entire batch is rejected.
493	- Only active blockages participate in cycle detection.
494	
495	---
496	
497	## `agt blockages resolve`
498	
499	Mark one or more blockages as resolved. The entries remain in the index for historical visibility.
500	
501	```bash
502	agt blockages resolve <blocked-id> --by <blocker-id> [<blocker-id> ...]
503	```
504	
505	**Arguments:**
506	
507	| Argument | Required | Description |
508	|----------|----------|-------------|
509	| `blocked-id` | Yes | The ID of the blocked issue |
510	| `--by` | Yes | One or more blocker IDs to resolve |
511	
512	**Example:**
513	
514	```bash
515	agt blockages resolve feature-x --by infra-setup
516	```
517	
518	**Output:**
519	
520	```json
521	{ "result": "OK" }
522	```
523	
524	---
525	
526	## `agt blockages delete`
527	
528	Remove one or more blockages entirely from the dependency index. Use when a blockage was added by mistake.
529	
530	```bash
531	agt blockages delete <blocked-id> --by <blocker-id> [<blocker-id> ...]
532	```
533	
534	**Arguments:**
535	
536	| Argument | Required | Description |
537	|----------|----------|-------------|
538	| `blocked-id` | Yes | The ID of the blocked issue |
539	| `--by` | Yes | One or more blocker IDs to delete |
540	
541	**Example:**
542	
543	```bash
544	agt blockages delete feature-x --by wrong-id
545	```
546	
547	**Output:**
548	
549	```json
550	{ "result": "OK" }
551	```
552	
553	**Notes:**
554	- Unlike resolve, delete removes the entry entirely from the index.
555	- A `blockage-deleted` event is still appended to the blocked issue for auditability.
556	
557	---
558	
559	## `agt blockages list`
560	
561	List all blockages for an issue -- both what blocks it and what it blocks.
562	
563	```bash
564	agt blockages list <issue-id>
565	```
566	
567	**Arguments:**
568	
569	| Argument | Required | Description |
570	|----------|----------|-------------|
571	| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |
572	
573	**Example:**
574	
575	```bash
576	agt blockages list feature-x
577	```
578	
579	**Output:**
580	
581	```json
582	{
583	  "issueId": "feature-x",
584	  "blockedBy": [
585	    { "blockerId": "infra-setup", "status": "active" },
586	    { "blockerId": "db-migration", "status": "resolved" }
587	  ],
588	  "blocks": [
589	    { "blockedId": "feature-y", "status": "active" }
590	  ]
591	}
592	```
593	
594	---
595	
596	## `agt users register`
597	
598	Register a new user and receive an authentication token.
599	
600	```bash
601	agt users register <name>
602	```
603	
604	**Arguments:**
605	
606	| Argument | Required | Description |
607	|----------|----------|-------------|
608	| `name` | Yes | Unique user name (case-insensitive, stored lowercase) |
609	
610	**Example:**
611	
612	```bash
613	agt users register alice
614	```
615	
616	**Output:**
617	
618	```json
619	{ "result": "OK", "name": "alice", "token": "tk_k7x2m9p4" }
620	```
621	
622	**Notes:**
623	- No token is required to run this command (it's how you obtain a token).
624	- The name `anonymous` is reserved.
625	- Save the returned token -- it won't be shown again.
626	
627	---
628	
629	## `agt users list`
630	
631	List all registered users. Tokens are not included.
632	
633	```bash
634	agt users list
635	```
636	
637	**Output:**
638	
639	```json
640	[
641	  { "name": "alice", "registeredAt": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z" },
642	  { "name": "bob", "registeredAt": "2025-01-16T14:30:00.000Z" }
643	]
644	```
645	
646	---
647	
648	## `agt users revoke`
649	
650	Revoke a user's token, removing their ability to authenticate.
651	
652	```bash
653	agt users revoke <name>
654	```
655	
656	**Arguments:**
657	
658	| Argument | Required | Description |
659	|----------|----------|-------------|
660	| `name` | Yes | The user name to revoke |
661	
662	**Example:**
663	
664	```bash
665	export AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN=tk_k7x2m9p4
666	agt users revoke bob
667	```
668	
669	**Output:**
670	
671	```json
672	{ "result": "OK" }
673	```
674	
675	**Notes:**
676	- Requires a valid token via `AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN`.
677	
678	---
679	
680	## `agt users regenerate`
681	
682	Generate a new token for an existing user, invalidating the old one.
683	
684	```bash
685	agt users regenerate <name>
686	```
687	
688	**Arguments:**
689	
690	| Argument | Required | Description |
691	|----------|----------|-------------|
692	| `name` | Yes | The user name to regenerate a token for |
693	
694	**Example:**
695	
696	```bash
697	export AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN=tk_k7x2m9p4
698	agt users regenerate alice
699	```
700	
701	**Output:**
702	
703	```json
704	{ "result": "OK", "name": "alice", "token": "tk_r5t1y8u2" }
705	```
706	
707	**Notes:**
708	- The `AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN` must contain the user's current token (self-service only).
709	
710	---
711	
712	## `agt push`
713	
714	Stage all changes in `.agentrack/`, auto-commit, and push to the remote `_agentrack` branch.
715	
716	```bash
717	agt push [--message <text>]
718	```
719	
720	**Flags:**
721	
722	| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
723	|------|------|---------|-------------|
724	| `--message` | string | `"sync: <ISO-8601>"` | Override the auto-generated commit message |
725	
726	**Example:**
727	
728	```bash
729	agt push
730	# { "result": "OK", "synced": true, "commitCount": 1 }
731	
732	agt push --message "Reviewed all open issues"
733	# { "result": "OK", "synced": true, "commitCount": 1 }
734	
735	agt push
736	# { "result": "OK", "synced": false, "message": "No changes to sync" }
737	```
738	
739	**Notes:**
740	- Requires `agt init` to have been run first.
741	- No authentication required -- operates on git directly.
742	
743	---
744	
745	## `agt pull`
746	
747	Pull the latest changes from the remote `_agentrack` branch.
748	
749	```bash
750	agt pull
751	```
752	
753	**Output:**
754	
755	```json
756	{ "result": "OK", "updated": true }
757	```
758	
759	Or if already up to date:
760	
761	```json
762	{ "result": "OK", "updated": false }
763	```
764	
765	**Notes:**
766	- Requires `agt init` to have been run first.
767	- No authentication required -- operates on git directly.
768	
769	---
770	
771	## Error codes
772	
773	### Global errors
774	
775	| Code | Meaning |
776	|------|---------|
777	| `NOT_INITIALIZED` | No `.agentrack/` directory found. Run `agt init`. |
778	| `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` | Current directory is not inside a git repository. |
779	| `MIGRATION_REQUIRED` | `.agentrack/` exists but is not a git worktree. Remove it and re-run `agt init`. |
780	| `INVALID_STATE` | Invalid state for the operation (e.g., currently on the `_agentrack` branch). |
781	| `PUSH_FAILED` | `agt push` failed. Error message includes git output. |
782	| `PULL_FAILED` | `agt pull` failed. Error message includes git output. |
783	| `TOKEN_REQUIRED` | A token is required by the current auth mode but none was provided. |
784	| `INVALID_TOKEN` | The provided token doesn't match any registered user. |
785	| `DEFAULT_USER_MISSING` | Auth mode is `open` but no `defaultUser` is configured. |
786	
787	### Issue errors
788	
789	| Code | Meaning |
790	|------|---------|
791	| `NOT_FOUND` | Issue with the given ID does not exist. |
792	| `ISSUE_MISSING` | Issue file is missing (deleted manually). Inconsistent state. |
793	
794	### Comment errors
795	
796	| Code | Meaning |
797	|------|---------|
798	| `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND` | Comment with the given ID doesn't exist or was already deleted. |
799	
800	### User errors
801	
802	| Code | Meaning |
803	|------|---------|
804	| `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS` | A user with that name is already registered. |
805	| `USER_NOT_FOUND` | No user with that name exists. |

# CLI reference

All agentrack CLI commands follow the format `agt <subcommand> [arguments] [flags]`. Commands output JSON to stdout. Errors output JSON to stderr with a non-zero exit code.

## Table of contents

- [init](#agt-init)
- [create](#agt-create)
- [update](#agt-update)
- [list](#agt-list)
- [view](#agt-view)
- [history](#agt-history)
- [next](#agt-next)
- [comments add](#agt-comments-add)
- [comments update](#agt-comments-update)
- [comments delete](#agt-comments-delete)
- [comments list](#agt-comments-list)
- [blockages add](#agt-blockages-add)
- [blockages resolve](#agt-blockages-resolve)
- [blockages delete](#agt-blockages-delete)
- [blockages list](#agt-blockages-list)
- [users register](#agt-users-register)
- [users list](#agt-users-list)
- [users revoke](#agt-users-revoke)
- [users regenerate](#agt-users-regenerate)
- [push](#agt-push)
- [pull](#agt-pull)
- [Error codes](#error-codes)

---

## `agt init`

Initialize the agentrack tracker in the current directory. Creates the `.agentrack/` directory on the `_agentrack` orphan branch.

```bash
agt init
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

If already initialized:

```json
{ "result": "ALREADY_INITIALIZED", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

**Notes:**
- Must be run inside a git repository.
- Idempotent -- running it again won't overwrite existing data.
- Handles two scenarios: creates a new orphan branch (fresh) or fetches an existing one (join). See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).

---

## `agt create`

Create a new issue.

```bash
agt create <title> [flags]
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | Yes | Short title for the issue |

**Flags:**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--description` | string | `""` | Detailed description |
| `--assignee` | string | `null` | User assigned to the issue |
| `--tags` | string | `""` | Comma-separated tags |
| `--status` | string | `"idea"` | Initial status: `idea`, `todo`, `in-progress`, `done`, `closed` |
| `--priority` | number | `3` | Priority 1 (critical) to 5 (trivial) |
| `--parentId` | string | `null` | Parent issue ID for hierarchy |
| `--path` | string | auto | Custom file path for the issue (relative to tracker dir) |

**Example:**

```bash
agt create "Fix login bug" \
  --description "SSO login returns 500 error" \
  --assignee alice \
  --tags "bug,auth" \
  --status todo \
  --priority 2
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "id": "m1x2k9ab" }
```

---

## `agt update`

Update an existing issue. At least one flag must be provided.

```bash
agt update <issue-id> [flags]
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue to update |

**Flags:**

| Flag | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `--title` | string | New title |
| `--description` | string | New description |
| `--status` | string | New status: `idea`, `todo`, `in-progress`, `done`, `closed` |
| `--assignee` | string | New assignee (use `null` to clear) |
| `--tags` | string | New comma-separated tags (replaces existing) |
| `--priority` | number | New priority 1-5 |
| `--parentId` | string | New parent ID (use `null` to detach) |

**Example:**

```bash
agt update m1x2k9ab --status in-progress --assignee bob
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

**Notes:**
- Updating status triggers hierarchy constraints. See [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md).
- Setting status to `done` or `closed` auto-resolves any active blockages where this issue is the blocker.

---

## `agt list`

List issues with optional filters. Returns items from the index (fast, doesn't read individual issue files).

```bash
agt list [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `--status` | string | Filter by status. Use `"open"` for all non-closed issues. |
| `--assignee` | string | Filter by assignee |
| `--tags` | string | Filter by tags (AND match -- issue must have all specified tags) |
| `--parentId` | string | Filter by parent ID. Use `null` for top-level issues. |

**Example:**

```bash
agt list --status open --assignee alice
```

**Output:**

```json
[
  {
    "id": "m1x2k9ab",
    "title": "Fix login bug",
    "status": "in-progress",
    "assignee": "alice",
    "tags": ["bug", "auth"],
    "parentId": null,
    "priority": 2
  }
]
```

**Notes:**
- Results are sorted by priority ascending, impact score descending, then `createdAt` ascending.
- The `path` field is intentionally excluded. Use `view` to get full issue details.

---

## `agt view`

Show the computed state of an issue by replaying its event log.

```bash
agt view <issue-id>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue to view |

**Example:**

```bash
agt view m1x2k9ab
```

**Output:**

```json
{
  "id": "m1x2k9ab",
  "title": "Fix login bug",
  "description": "SSO login returns 500 error",
  "status": "in-progress",
  "assignee": "alice",
  "tags": ["bug", "auth"],
  "parentId": null,
  "priority": 2,
  "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z",
  "createdBy": "alice",
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-15T11:00:00.000Z"
}
```

---

## `agt history`

Show the raw event log for an issue.

```bash
agt history <issue-id>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |

**Example:**

```bash
agt history m1x2k9ab
```

**Output:**

```json
[
  { "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z", "type": "creation", "author": "alice" },
  {
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z",
    "type": "update",
    "author": "alice",
    "content": {
      "title": "Fix login bug",
      "description": "SSO login returns 500 error",
      "status": "todo",
      "assignee": "alice",
      "tags": ["bug", "auth"],
      "priority": 2
    }
  },
  {
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T11:00:00.000Z",
    "type": "update",
    "author": "alice",
    "content": { "status": "in-progress" }
  }
]
```

See [The issue object](./issue-object.md) for the event sourcing model.

---

## `agt next`

Recommend the next issue for a given user. Returns the highest-priority, unblocked issue assigned to that user, sorted by impact score and creation date.

```bash
agt next <user>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `user` | Yes | The assignee name to find the next issue for |

**Example:**

```bash
agt next alice
```

**Output:**

```json
{
  "id": "m1x2k9ab",
  "title": "Fix login bug",
  "description": "SSO login returns 500 error",
  "status": "todo",
  "assignee": "alice",
  "tags": ["bug", "auth"],
  "parentId": null,
  "priority": 2,
  "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z",
  "createdBy": "alice",
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z"
}
```

If no issues are available:

```json
{ "result": "NO_ISSUES_AVAILABLE", "message": "No unblocked issues found for alice" }
```

---

## `agt comments add`

Add a comment to an issue.

```bash
agt comments add <issue-id> --content <text>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |
| `--content` | Yes | The comment text |

**Example:**

```bash
agt comments add m1x2k9ab --content "Found the root cause: expired SSO certificate"
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "commentId": "c1a2b3d4" }
```

---

## `agt comments update`

Edit an existing comment. The original comment event is preserved; a new `comment-update` event is appended.

```bash
agt comments update <issue-id> <comment-id> --content <text>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |
| `comment-id` | Yes | The ID of the comment to update |
| `--content` | Yes | The new comment text |

**Example:**

```bash
agt comments update m1x2k9ab c1a2b3d4 --content "Root cause was expired SSO certificate, now renewed"
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

---

## `agt comments delete`

Delete a comment. The original event is preserved; a `comment-delete` event is appended. Deleted comments are excluded from `comments list` output.

```bash
agt comments delete <issue-id> <comment-id>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |
| `comment-id` | Yes | The ID of the comment to delete |

**Example:**

```bash
agt comments delete m1x2k9ab c1a2b3d4
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

---

## `agt comments list`

List all active (non-deleted) comments for an issue, with edits applied.

```bash
agt comments list <issue-id>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |

**Example:**

```bash
agt comments list m1x2k9ab
```

**Output:**

```json
[
  {
    "id": "c1a2b3d4",
    "author": "alice",
    "content": "Root cause was expired SSO certificate, now renewed",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
    "editedAt": "2025-01-15T10:35:00.000Z"
  },
  {
    "id": "e5f6g7h8",
    "author": "bob",
    "content": "Verified fix in staging",
    "timestamp": "2025-01-15T11:00:00.000Z"
  }
]
```

---

## `agt blockages add`

Block an issue by one or more other issues. Multiple blockers can be specified for atomic dependency creation.

```bash
agt blockages add <blocked-id> --by <blocker-id> [<blocker-id> ...]
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `blocked-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue to block |
| `--by` | Yes | One or more blocker IDs |

**Example:**

```bash
# Single blocker
agt blockages add feature-x --by infra-setup

# Multiple blockers (atomic -- all or nothing)
agt blockages add feature-x --by infra-setup db-migration config-update
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

**Notes:**
- Cycle detection runs for each blocker. If any would create a cycle, the entire batch is rejected.
- Only active blockages participate in cycle detection.

---

## `agt blockages resolve`

Mark one or more blockages as resolved. The entries remain in the index for historical visibility.

```bash
agt blockages resolve <blocked-id> --by <blocker-id> [<blocker-id> ...]
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `blocked-id` | Yes | The ID of the blocked issue |
| `--by` | Yes | One or more blocker IDs to resolve |

**Example:**

```bash
agt blockages resolve feature-x --by infra-setup
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

---

## `agt blockages delete`

Remove one or more blockages entirely from the dependency index. Use when a blockage was added by mistake.

```bash
agt blockages delete <blocked-id> --by <blocker-id> [<blocker-id> ...]
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `blocked-id` | Yes | The ID of the blocked issue |
| `--by` | Yes | One or more blocker IDs to delete |

**Example:**

```bash
agt blockages delete feature-x --by wrong-id
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

**Notes:**
- Unlike resolve, delete removes the entry entirely from the index.
- A `blockage-deleted` event is still appended to the blocked issue for auditability.

---

## `agt blockages list`

List all blockages for an issue -- both what blocks it and what it blocks.

```bash
agt blockages list <issue-id>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `issue-id` | Yes | The ID of the issue |

**Example:**

```bash
agt blockages list feature-x
```

**Output:**

```json
{
  "issueId": "feature-x",
  "blockedBy": [
    { "blockerId": "infra-setup", "status": "active" },
    { "blockerId": "db-migration", "status": "resolved" }
  ],
  "blocks": [
    { "blockedId": "feature-y", "status": "active" }
  ]
}
```

---

## `agt users register`

Register a new user and receive an authentication token.

```bash
agt users register <name>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Unique user name (case-insensitive, stored lowercase) |

**Example:**

```bash
agt users register alice
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "name": "alice", "token": "tk_k7x2m9p4" }
```

**Notes:**
- No token is required to run this command (it's how you obtain a token).
- The name `anonymous` is reserved.
- Save the returned token -- it won't be shown again.

---

## `agt users list`

List all registered users. Tokens are not included.

```bash
agt users list
```

**Output:**

```json
[
  { "name": "alice", "registeredAt": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z" },
  { "name": "bob", "registeredAt": "2025-01-16T14:30:00.000Z" }
]
```

---

## `agt users revoke`

Revoke a user's token, removing their ability to authenticate.

```bash
agt users revoke <name>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | The user name to revoke |

**Example:**

```bash
export AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN=tk_k7x2m9p4
agt users revoke bob
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK" }
```

**Notes:**
- Requires a valid token via `AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN`.

---

## `agt users regenerate`

Generate a new token for an existing user, invalidating the old one.

```bash
agt users regenerate <name>
```

**Arguments:**

| Argument | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | The user name to regenerate a token for |

**Example:**

```bash
export AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN=tk_k7x2m9p4
agt users regenerate alice
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "name": "alice", "token": "tk_r5t1y8u2" }
```

**Notes:**
- The `AGENTACK_USER_TOKEN` must contain the user's current token (self-service only).

---

## `agt push`

Stage all changes in `.agentrack/`, auto-commit, and push to the remote `_agentrack` branch.

```bash
agt push [--message <text>]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--message` | string | `"sync: <ISO-8601>"` | Override the auto-generated commit message |

**Example:**

```bash
agt push
# { "result": "OK", "synced": true, "commitCount": 1 }

agt push --message "Reviewed all open issues"
# { "result": "OK", "synced": true, "commitCount": 1 }

agt push
# { "result": "OK", "synced": false, "message": "No changes to sync" }
```

**Notes:**
- Requires `agt init` to have been run first.
- No authentication required -- operates on git directly.

---

## `agt pull`

Pull the latest changes from the remote `_agentrack` branch.

```bash
agt pull
```

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "updated": true }
```

Or if already up to date:

```json
{ "result": "OK", "updated": false }
```

**Notes:**
- Requires `agt init` to have been run first.
- No authentication required -- operates on git directly.

---

## Error codes

### Global errors

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `NOT_INITIALIZED` | No `.agentrack/` directory found. Run `agt init`. |
| `NOT_A_GIT_REPO` | Current directory is not inside a git repository. |
| `MIGRATION_REQUIRED` | `.agentrack/` exists but is not a git worktree. Remove it and re-run `agt init`. |
| `INVALID_STATE` | Invalid state for the operation (e.g., currently on the `_agentrack` branch). |
| `PUSH_FAILED` | `agt push` failed. Error message includes git output. |
| `PULL_FAILED` | `agt pull` failed. Error message includes git output. |
| `TOKEN_REQUIRED` | A token is required by the current auth mode but none was provided. |
| `INVALID_TOKEN` | The provided token doesn't match any registered user. |
| `DEFAULT_USER_MISSING` | Auth mode is `open` but no `defaultUser` is configured. |

### Issue errors

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `NOT_FOUND` | Issue with the given ID does not exist. |
| `ISSUE_MISSING` | Issue file is missing (deleted manually). Inconsistent state. |

### Comment errors

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND` | Comment with the given ID doesn't exist or was already deleted. |

### User errors

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS` | A user with that name is already registered. |
| `USER_NOT_FOUND` | No user with that name exists. |

## See also

- [Getting started](./getting-started.md) -- First session walkthrough
- [Authentication](./authentication.md) -- Token setup and auth modes
- [The issue object](./issue-object.md) -- Issue properties and status lifecycle
- [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md) -- Dependency management
- [JavaScript reference](./javascript-reference.md) -- Programmatic API

# Storing issues in git

Agentrack stores all tracker data in a `.agentrack/` directory that lives on its own git branch, separate from your code. This approach gives you the benefits of git-based storage (version history, distributed sync, no server) without the downsides (merge conflicts with code changes, cluttering your working tree).

## How it works

When you run `agt init`, agentrack:

1. Creates a git worktree -- a separate checkout of the repository at `.agentrack/` that points to an orphan branch called `_agentrack`.
2. Sets up the directory structure inside the worktree.
3. Adds `.agentrack/` to your main branch's `.gitignore` so it doesn't interfere with your code.

The `_agentrack` branch has no shared history with your code branches. It's a completely independent branch that only contains tracker data.

```
Your repo/
  main branch:        src/, package.json, .gitignore (includes .agentrack/)
  _agentrack branch:  .agentrack/ (index.json, config.json, issues/, etc.)
```

This means:
- **No merge conflicts** -- Issue files never conflict with code files because they live on different branches.
- **Branch-independent access** -- You can read and write issues from any code branch.
- **Standard git sync** -- Push and pull use regular git operations.

## Directory structure

The `.agentrack/` directory contains:

```
.agentrack/
  config.json          # Auth mode, default user
  index.json           # Issue index (open + closed arrays, childrenOf map)
  dependencies.json    # Blockage relationships (blockedBy + blocks maps)
  users.json           # Registered users and tokens
  issues/
    m1x2k9ab.json      # Event log for issue m1x2k9ab
    def456gh.json      # Event log for issue def456gh
    ...
```

### config.json

Global configuration, created by `agt init`:

```json
{
  "auth": {
    "mode": "read-only",
    "defaultUser": "anonymous"
  }
}
```

See [Authentication](./authentication.md) for auth mode details.

### index.json

The issue index with two sorted arrays and a hierarchy map:

```json
{
  "open": [
    { "id": "m1x2k9ab", "title": "Fix login bug", "status": "todo", "assignee": "alice", "parentId": null, "tags": ["bug"], "priority": 2 }
  ],
  "closed": [],
  "childrenOf": {}
}
```

The index enables fast lookups without reading individual issue files. See [The issue object](./issue-object.md) for field descriptions.

### dependencies.json

Bidirectional blockage map:

```json
{
  "blockedBy": {
    "feat1": [{ "blockerId": "infra1", "status": "active" }]
  },
  "blocks": {
    "infra1": [{ "blockedId": "feat1", "status": "active" }]
  }
}
```

See [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md) for how blockages work.

### users.json

User registry with tokens:

```json
{
  "users": [
    { "name": "alice", "token": "tk_k7x2m9p4", "registeredAt": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z" }
  ]
}
```

See [Authentication](./authentication.md) for user management.

### Issue files

Each issue is a JSON file containing an array of events:

```json
[
  { "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z", "type": "creation", "author": "alice" },
  { "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:00:00.000Z", "type": "update", "author": "alice", "content": { "title": "Fix login bug", "status": "todo" } },
  { "timestamp": "2025-01-15T11:00:00.000Z", "type": "update", "author": "bob", "content": { "status": "in-progress" } }
]
```

See [The issue object](./issue-object.md) for the event sourcing model.

## Syncing with remote

Since issues live on a git branch, you use standard git operations to sync between machines and team members. Agentrack provides two commands for this.

### `agt push` -- Sync to remote

Stage all changes in `.agentrack/`, auto-commit, and push to the remote `_agentrack` branch:

```bash
agt push
# { "result": "OK", "synced": true, "commitCount": 1 }

agt push --message "Reviewed all open issues"
# { "result": "OK", "synced": true, "commitCount": 1 }
```

If there are no changes:

```bash
agt push
# { "result": "OK", "synced": false, "message": "No changes to sync" }
```

### `agt pull` -- Sync from remote

Pull the latest changes from the remote `_agentrack` branch:

```bash
agt pull
# { "result": "OK", "updated": true }

agt pull
# { "result": "OK", "updated": false }  # already up to date
```

In JavaScript:

```javascript
import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
const tracker = new Tracker();

// Push local changes to remote
const result = await tracker.pushWorktree(cwd);
// { synced: true, commitCount: 1 }

// Pull remote changes
const pullResult = await tracker.pullWorktree(cwd);
// { updated: true }
```

## Init scenarios

`agt init` handles two scenarios automatically:

### Fresh setup

When no `_agentrack` branch exists on the remote:

```bash
agt init
# Creates a new orphan branch, sets up the directory, pushes to remote
# { "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

### Joining an existing setup

When the remote already has an `_agentrack` branch (e.g., a teammate already initialized the tracker):

```bash
agt init
# Fetches the existing branch, checks out the worktree
# { "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

In both cases, the result is the same: a `.agentrack/` directory ready to use.

## Resolution order

Agentrack resolves the `.agentrack/` directory by walking up from the current working directory:

1. Check `cwd/.agentrack/` -- if it exists, use it.
2. Check `parent/.agentrack/` -- if it exists, use it.
3. Continue walking up until reaching the filesystem root.
4. If no `.agentrack/` is found, return a `NOT_INITIALIZED` error.

This means you can run `agt` commands from any subdirectory in your project. It also supports monorepos -- different subdirectories can have their own `.agentrack/` trackers.

## Team workflow example

Here's how a team of agents collaborates using git sync:

```bash
# Agent 1: Create issues and push
agt create "Implement user auth" --status todo --assignee coder
agt create "Write auth tests" --status todo --assignee tester
agt push

# Agent 2: Pull and start working
agt pull
agt update m1x2k9ab --status in-progress
agt push

# Agent 3: Pull and add comments
agt pull
agt comments add m1x2k9ab --content "Use JWT for session management"
agt push

# Agent 1: Pull to see updates
agt pull
agt list --status open
```

The worktree approach means agents can read and write concurrently without blocking each other, similar to how git handles concurrent edits on different branches.

## See also

- [Getting started](./getting-started.md) -- Running `agt init` and your first session
- [The issue object](./issue-object.md) -- What's stored in issue files
- [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md) -- What's in `dependencies.json`
- [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md) -- `agt init`, `agt push`, `agt pull` commands
- [JavaScript reference](./javascript-reference.md) -- Worktree functions and the Tracker class

2	
3	Agentrack is a lightweight issue tracker designed for AI agents and developers who work in git repositories. It stores issues as JSON files on a dedicated git branch, so your tracker data lives alongside your code without generating merge conflicts.
4	
5	## Why agentrack?
6	
7	Traditional issue trackers (Jira, GitHub Issues, Linear) are built around web interfaces and human workflows. Agentrack is different:
8	
9	- **File-backed** -- All data lives in JSON files. No database, no server, no infrastructure.
10	- **Event-sourced** -- Every change is an immutable event. The current state of an issue is computed by replaying its event log, so you always have a full audit trail.
11	- **Git-friendly** -- Issues are stored on a dedicated orphan branch (`_agentrack`) via git worktree. Push and pull with standard git commands. No merge conflicts with your code.
12	- **Designed for AI agents** -- The CLI outputs JSON by default, making it easy for agents and scripts to parse. The JavaScript API gives full programmatic access.
13	- **Zero infrastructure** -- `npm install agentrack` and you're done. No accounts, no hosting, no configuration servers.
14	- **Multi-agent ready** -- Token-based authentication lets multiple agents (and humans) attribute their actions. Choose from open, read-only, or strict auth modes.
15	
16	## Key features
17	
18	### Event sourcing
19	
20	Every action on an issue -- creating it, changing its status, adding a comment, linking a dependency -- is recorded as an immutable event. The current state is always computed by replaying the event log from start to finish. This means you never lose history, and you can always understand how an issue evolved.
21	
22	### Hierarchy and dependencies
23	
24	Issues can form parent-child trees via the `parentId` property, and they can declare dependencies via blockages. The hierarchy enforces status constraints: a parent can't be closed until its children are done, and starting work on a child automatically promotes the parent. Blockages prevent work from starting until blockers are resolved. See [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md).
25	
26	### Git-native storage
27	
28	Instead of a database, agentrack stores everything in JSON files on a dedicated git branch. This means your issues are versioned, distributed, and synced alongside your code -- but without merge conflicts. See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).
29	
30	### Token-based auth
31	
32	Multiple agents can register as users and attribute their actions via lightweight tokens. Three auth modes (open, read-only, strict) let you balance convenience and accountability. See [Authentication](./authentication.md).
33	
34	### Priority and impact scoring
35	
36	Issues have a priority from 1 (critical) to 5 (trivial). When listing or getting the next issue, agentrack sorts by priority, then by impact score (how many other issues depend on this one), then by age. This helps agents automatically pick the most important work. See [The issue object](./issue-object.md).
37	
38	## Two ways to use it
39	
40	Agentrack provides two interfaces for the same underlying tracker:
41	
42	1. **CLI** -- The `agt` command-line tool. Ideal for quick interactions, scripting, and agent tool use.
43	
44	   ```bash
45	   agt create "Fix login bug" --status todo --assignee "alice" --priority 2
46	   ```
47	
48	2. **JavaScript API** -- The `Tracker` class. Ideal for application integration, custom workflows, and batch operations.
49	
50	   ```javascript
51	   import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
52	
53	   const tracker = new Tracker();
54	   const { id } = await tracker.create({
55	     title: "Fix login bug",
56	     status: "todo",
57	     assignee: "alice",
58	     priority: 2,
59	   });
60	   ```
61	
62	## Quick example
63	
64	Here's a complete workflow in three steps:
65	
66	```bash
67	# 1. Initialize the tracker in your repository
68	agt init
69	
70	# 2. Create an issue
71	agt create "Set up CI pipeline" --status todo --tags "devops,infra"
72	
73	# 3. View all open issues
74	agt list --status open
75	```
76	
77	The equivalent in JavaScript:
78	
79	```javascript
80	import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
81	const tracker = new Tracker();
82	
83	await tracker.init();
84	const { id } = await tracker.create({
85	  title: "Set up CI pipeline",
86	  status: "todo",
87	  tags: ["devops", "infra"],
88	});
89	const issues = await tracker.list({ status: "open" });
90	```
91	
92	## Status lifecycle
93	
94	Issues progress through five statuses:
95	
96	```
97	idea --> todo --> in-progress --> done --> closed
98	```
99	
100	- **idea** -- A thought or proposal, not yet committed to.
101	- **todo** -- Accepted and planned, ready to be picked up.
102	- **in-progress** -- Someone is actively working on it.
103	- **done** -- Work is complete, awaiting review or verification.
104	- **closed** -- Final state. Resolved, abandoned, or no longer relevant.
105	
106	The `--status open` filter matches everything except `closed`.
107	
108	## What's next?
109	
110	- [Getting started](./getting-started.md) -- Install agentrack and run through your first session
111	- [Authentication](./authentication.md) -- Set up users and tokens for multi-agent workflows
112	- [The issue object](./issue-object.md) -- Properties, status lifecycle, and the event sourcing model
113	- [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md) -- Parent-child relationships and dependency tracking
114	- [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md) -- How agentrack uses git branches to store tracker data
115	- [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md) -- Complete command documentation
116	- [JavaScript reference](./javascript-reference.md) -- Tracker class methods and exported types

Blockages prevent work from starting until blockers are resolved. See [Hierarchy and blockages](./hierarchy-and-blockages.md).

### Git-native storage

Instead of a database, agentrack stores everything in JSON files on a dedicated git branch. This means your issues are versioned, distributed, and synced alongside your code -- but without merge conflicts. See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).

### Token-based auth

Multiple agents can register as users and attribute their actions via lightweight tokens. Three auth modes (open, read-only, strict) let you balance convenience and accountability. See [Authentication](./authentication.md).

### Priority and impact scoring

Issues have a priority from 1 (critical) to 5 (trivial). When listing or getting the next issue, agentrack sorts by priority, then by impact score (how many other issues depend on this one), then by age. This helps agents automatically pick the most important work. See [The issue object](./issue-object.md).

## Two ways to use it

Agentrack provides two interfaces for the same underlying tracker:

1. **CLI** -- The `agt` command-line tool. Ideal for quick interactions, scripting, and agent tool use.

   ```bash
   agt create "Fix login bug" --status todo --assignee "alice" --priority 2
   ```

2. **JavaScript API** -- The `Tracker` class. Ideal for application integration, custom workflows, and batch operations.

   ```javascript
   import { Tracker } from "agentrack";

   const tracker = new Tracker();
   const { id } = await tracker.create({
     title: "Fix login bug",
     status: "todo",
     assignee: "alice",
     priority: 2,
   });
   ```

## Quick example

Here's a complete workflow in three steps:

```bash
# 1. Initialize the tracker in your repository
agt init

# 2. Create an issue
agt create "Set up CI pipeline" --status todo --tags "devops,infra"

# 3. View all open issues
agt list --status open
```

The equivalent in JavaScript:

```javascript
import { Tracker } from "agentrack";
const tracker = new Tracker();

await tracker.init();
const { id } = await tracker.create({
  title: "Set up CI pipeline",
  status: "todo",
  tags: ["devops", "infra"],
});
const issues = await tracker.list({ status: "open" });
```

## Status lifecycle

Issues progress through five statuses:

```
idea --> todo --> in-progress --> done --> closed
```

- **idea** -- A thought or proposal, not yet committed to.
- **todo** -- Accepted and planned, ready to be picked up.
- **in-progress** -- Someone is actively working on it.
- **done** -- Work is complete, awaiting review or verification.
- **closed** -- Final state. Resolved, abandoned, or no longer relevant.

The `--status open` filter matches everything except `closed`.

## `agt init`

Initialize the agentrack tracker in the current directory. Creates a worktree directory on an orphan branch.

```bash
agt init [--branch <name>]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--branch` | string | `_agentrack` | Name for the orphan branch and worktree directory |

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

If already initialized:

```json
{ "result": "ALREADY_INITIALIZED", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

### Branch normalization

The `--branch` flag accepts a friendly name that is normalized into a git branch name and directory name:

1. Leading underscores are stripped from the input
2. An underscore is prepended for the branch name, a dot for the directory name

| Flag value | Branch name | Directory name |
|------------|-------------|----------------|
| (none)     | `_agentrack` | `.agentrack/` |
| `testing`  | `_testing`   | `.testing/` |
| `_ci`      | `_ci`        | `.ci/` |
| `myproject`| `_myproject` | `.myproject/` |

This means `--branch testing` and `--branch _testing` produce the same result.

### Examples

```bash
# Default: branch _agentrack, directory .agentrack/
agt init

# Custom branch for a dedicated test instance
agt init --branch testing
# Creates branch _testing, directory .testing/

# Multiple instances in one repo (each on its own branch)
agt init --branch frontend
agt init --branch backend
```

### Pointer file

After `agt init`, a pointer file (`.agentrack.json`) is created at the repository root. This file records the active branch name so that all subsequent commands (`push`, `pull`, etc.) know which worktree directory to use:

```json
{
  "branch": "_testing"
}
```

For backward compatibility, if `.agentrack.json` does not exist, commands assume the default branch (`_agentrack`) and directory (`.agentrack/`).

### Notes

- Must be run inside a git repository.
- Idempotent -- running it again won't overwrite existing data.
- Branch names cannot contain slashes (they would create nested directories). Use dashes instead: `--branch feature-test`.
- Handles two scenarios: creates a new orphan branch (fresh) or fetches an existing one (join). See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).

# CTO Expertise Index
# Agent: cto
# Domain: Project architecture, technical specifications, development alignment

hierarchy:
  manager: none — top-level agent
  subordinates:
    active:
      - library-developer (implementation)
      - library-validator (testing, quality gates — documentation removed)
      - library-releaser (release prep, documentation, build, version management, publishing)

expertise_status: "Dogfooding active. Active chains: --branch flag implementation (mpfm8bilwf, in-progress) — implementation mpfm9aff8v done but validation found 2 critical bugs (double directory creation, missing BRANCH_CONFLICT). Fix issue mpfn4dkotn (library-developer, priority 1) created. Validation re-run mpfm9ixr9i blocked on fix. Docs mpfm9qxpsd still blocked on validation. Key lesson: always rebuild dist/ before validating CLI changes. E2E validation suite (mpebmstgs9, in-progress). Standing issues: defensive index validation (mp3pe95w9e), concurrent writes decision (mp3pe96e9f), CLAUDE.md decision (mp3pe9urb9). Future: Docusaurus site (mpdxdbqwt9, idea). Public docs at docs/markdown/ (8 files) — all agents have read access."

project_overview:
  name: agentrack
  previous_name: trackgentic (renamed 2026-05-18)
  type: npm library (TypeScript, Bun runtime)
  purpose: Issue tracker designed for AI agents — file-backed, event-sourced, git-friendly
  distribution: npm package with CLI entry point (`agt` command)
  stage: "Dogfooding active. Project renamed from trackgentic to agentrack. .trackgentic/ → .agentrack/, CLI command tg → agt. npm link must be re-run from packages/library/ to restore global symlink. Shipped features: independent git branch (worktree-based storage on orphan _agentrack branch). In-progress: configurable branch name (--branch flag on agt init, mpfm8bilwf) — implemented but validation found 2 critical bugs (double directory creation, missing BRANCH_CONFLICT), fix in progress (mpfn4dkotn). Standing issues: defensive index validation (mp3pe95w9e), concurrent writes decision (mp3pe96e9f), CLAUDE.md decision (mp3pe9urb9). E2E validation suite in progress (mpebmstgs9)."
  bun_version: "1.3.11"
  build_tool: tsup (implemented, producing dist/)
  docs_tool: "Hand-written markdown docs in docs/markdown/ (8 sections). TypeDoc removed. Docs overhaul in progress (mpdpt4rego), validation pending (mpdpv6gw49). Future: Docusaurus site consuming docs/markdown/ (mpdxdbqwt9, idea). Spec: .agentic/specs/user-docs-spec.md."

detail_files:
  - path: architecture.yaml
    description: Core data model, file structure, event sourcing, resolution algorithm, index design
  - path: design-decisions.yaml
    description: Architectural decisions and rationale (why file-backed, why event-sourced, etc.)
  - path: status.yaml
    description: Current project status, implementation roadmap, open questions, risks

specifications:
  location: .agentic/specs/
  files:
    - path: 01-overview.md
      description: Monorepo structure, library package layout, design principles, dependencies, CLI/API relationship
    - path: 02-data-model.md
      description: All TypeScript types, interfaces, file formats, initial file contents
    - path: 03-api-specification.md
      description: Every Tracker method with params, return types, behavior, error handling
    - path: 04-cli-specification.md
      description: Every CLI command with args, flags, auth, output format, error handling
    - path: 05-implementation-phases.md
      description: 7 phases from foundation to polish, with tasks, tests, and exit criteria per phase
    - path: 06-quality-plan.md
      description: Quality plan — now uses Prettier + ESLint (was Biome). Linting, typechecking (strict+), testing (Bun), test organization, documentation (TypeDoc), quality gates
    - path: 07-phase3-auth-users.md
      description: Phase 3 specification — auth module (resolveAuthor), user CRUD (register/list/revoke/regenerate), auth integration into existing methods, CLI user commands
    - path: 07-phase4-comments-spec.md
      description: Phase 4 specification — computeComments function, 4 Tracker comment methods, CLI comment commands, test plan
    - path: 08-phase5-hierarchy-spec.md
      description: Phase 5 specification — childrenOf map management, hierarchy.ts (upward/downward constraints), Tracker create/update integration, reparenting, test plan
    - path: 07-phase6-blockages-spec.md
      description: Phase 6 specification — dependency-manager (bidirectional maps, cycle detection, batch atomicity, impact score), 4 Tracker blockage methods, auto-resolution on status change, CLI blockage commands, test plan
    - path: 08-phase7-polish-spec.md
      description: Phase 7 specification — JSDoc on all public API, error message polish, edge case & resilience testing, package configuration verification
    - path: next-command-spec.md
      description: "`next <user-name>` command — recommend highest-priority unblocked issue for a user. Returns ComputedIssue or NO_ISSUES_AVAILABLE. Filters by assignee, actionable statuses (idea/todo/in-progress), no active blockages. Sort: priority ASC → impact DESC → id ASC."
    - path: next-todo-only-spec.md
      description: "Amends next-command-spec: restrict status filter from [idea, todo, in-progress] to [todo] only. Single-line change in Tracker.next(). REVIEWED — reviews skipped (trivially scoped). Implementation mp9zda04cp in-progress with library-developer."
    - path: cap-upward-promotion-spec.md
      description: "Cap upward auto-promotion at in-progress. Parents never auto-promote to done/closed via computeUpwardPromotions. Spec status: REVIEWED. Reason format: auto-promoted to TARGET: child advanced to CHILD. 7 new test cases required."
    - path: independent-git-spec.md
      description: "Store .agentrack/ on orphan branch _agentrack via git worktree. Branch-independent issue access. Two init scenarios (fresh/join). Three commands: agt init (worktree setup), agt push (auto-commit + sync), agt pull (sync from remote). New module src/worktree.ts + 2 new CLI commands. Status: IMPLEMENTED with 3 spec deviations found in validation. Fix phase: mpd4hktoxq (fix deviations) → mpd4hs14zp (validate + tests) → mpd4i06wz6 (document + build). Parent: mpcwcufhzk."
      naming_conventions: "Branch = `_agentrack`, directory = `.agentrack`, tool = `agentrack`, data inside branch = `issues/`"
    - path: docs-generation.md
      description: "SUPERSEDED by user-docs-spec.md. TypeDoc dual-format docs are being removed. Release workflow and .gitignore updated by CTO (mpdpvfn3yb done). Typedoc tooling cleanup pending (mpdpu00ksc)."
    - path: user-docs-spec.md
      description: "User-friendly documentation overhaul. Replace TypeDoc auto-generated docs with hand-written markdown in docs/markdown/. 8 sections: overview, getting started, authentication, issue object, hierarchy & blockages, storing in git, CLI reference, JS reference. Removes typedoc tooling entirely. Parent: mpdpt4rego. CTO config (mpdpvfn3yb) done. TypeDoc deps removed from package.json. Doc writing: mpdwq7dvls (library-releaser, replaces failed mpdpuhd0r5)."
    - path: configurable-branch-spec.md
      description: "Configurable branch name for agt init. --branch <name> flag allows custom orphan branch per agentrack instance. Normalization: strip leading _, prepend _ for branch, . for dir. Pointer file (.agentrack.json) at repo root solves circular discovery. Slash rejection (AC8). resolution.ts and tracker.ts dynamic discovery via pointer file. New module: src/core/pointer.ts (actually implemented as branch-config.ts). Enables multiple instances per repo and test isolation. IMPLEMENTED (mpfm9aff8v) but validation (mpfm9ixr9i) found 2 critical bugs: (1) double directory creation — tracker init runs before branch flag takes effect, leaving stale .agentrack/ alongside custom dir, (2) missing BRANCH_CONFLICT detection. Fix: mpfn4dkotn (library-developer). Parent: mpfm8bilwf. Spec status: REVIEWED."
    - path: e2e-validation-suite-spec.md
      description: "E2E test suite in validation/ folder. Uses real git repos + agt CLI invocations (spawn + capture). Covers all CLI commands with happy/error/edge cases. Full lifecycle test. No library code changes. Parent: mpebmstgs9. Implementation: mpebnnq5qq (library-validator)."

access_boundaries:

  cto_scope: ".agentic/ files, root-level config, specifications, expertise files"
  code_access: "If code-level insight is needed, ask library-developer or library-validator to report — never read source directly."

delegation_workflow:
  mandatory_sequence: |
    After every library-developer delegation that makes code changes, you MUST delegate to library-validator for validation.
    Sequence: library-developer (implement) → library-validator (validate).
    Never skip the quality validation step. This ensures code is clean, tested, and documented.
  timeout_constraint: |
    Bash tool has a 10-minute (600000ms) timeout. Large phases must be split into sub-delegations of ~5-8 minutes each.
    Split strategy for Phase 3: (A) auth.ts + errors.ts, (B) user methods in tracker.ts, (C) auth integration into existing methods + CLI commands, (D) library-validator validation).
    Each sub-task should be scoped to a few files to stay within timeout.
  docs_ownership: |
    library-releaser owns documentation tasks: TypeDoc configuration, doc generation, docs scripts.
    When docs need updating or generating for a release, delegate to library-releaser.
    library-validator no longer handles documentation — only testing and quality gates.
  api_change_policy: |
    MANDATORY: Any change to CLI command behavior or to the API of public functions must be
    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.
    ENFORCEMENT: Every /issue chain that touches CLI or public API MUST include a library-releaser
    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.
    Violation caught in session 68: configurable-branch shipped without docs+build task.
  docs_awareness: |
    All agents have read access to docs/markdown/ (8 files: overview, getting-started, authentication,
    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.
  access_gaps: |
    Resolved: user granted CTO access to .github/ folder. CTO now owns workflow files.
    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.
  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."
  library-developer:
    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."
  library-validator:
    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:
    focus: "Delegate release tasks: verify quality gates pass, generate documentation (HTML + Markdown), build artifacts, bump version, publish to npm. Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

  - docs/issue-blockages.md — dependency index, blockage lifecycle, cycle detection, impact scoring

    delegated to library-releaser for running the build and updating documentation.
    This applies to ALL code changes that touch public-facing surface area — whether new features,
    behavioral changes, or signature modifications. library-releaser must rebuild dist/ and update
    docs/markdown/ to reflect the change before the work is considered complete.

    task as part of the issue chain. Do NOT mark the parent as done until library-releaser completes.
    Violation caught in session 68: configurable-branch shipped without docs+build task.
  docs_awareness: |

    issue-object, hierarchy-and-blockages, storing-issues-in-git, cli-reference, javascript-reference).
    Agents can consult these docs for API details, CLI usage patterns, and feature behavior.
    library-releaser has docs_structure in its expertise file with full file listing.
    When delegating tasks, mention docs/ availability if the agent might benefit from reference material.
  access_gaps: |

    Root .gitignore is also writable by CTO.
  note: "Self-check and validation steps are enforced via agent system prompts. No need to duplicate in delegation messages."
  library-developer:
    focus: "Focus delegation messages on the implementation task itself. The agent self-checks typecheck+lint+test before completion."
  library-validator:
    focus: "Always pass the same spec file used for implementation so quality can validate alignment with specs, not just code quality. Include the spec path, what changed, and what behaviors to validate. Handles testing and quality gates only (documentation moved to library-releaser)."
  library-releaser:
    focus: "Delegate release tasks: verify quality gates pass, generate documentation (HTML + Markdown), build artifacts, bump version, publish to npm. Provide version bump guidance (patch/minor/major) based on changes since last release. The agent owns the full release lifecycle end-to-end. Docs output: docs/html/ (users) + docs/md/ (agents) at repo root. Agent has docs/** access for writing generated documentation."

tool_input.new_string:
## `agt init`

Initialize the agentrack tracker in the current directory. Creates a worktree directory on an orphan branch.

```bash
agt init [--branch <name>]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--branch` | string | `_agentrack` | Name for the orphan branch and worktree directory |

**Output:**

```json
{ "result": "OK", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

If already initialized:

```json
{ "result": "ALREADY_INITIALIZED", "path": "/path/to/project" }
```

### Branch normalization

The `--branch` flag accepts a friendly name that is normalized into a git branch name and directory name:

1. Leading underscores are stripped from the input
2. An underscore is prepended for the branch name, a dot for the directory name

| Flag value | Branch name | Directory name |
|------------|-------------|----------------|
| (none)     | `_agentrack` | `.agentrack/` |
| `testing`  | `_testing`   | `.testing/` |
| `_ci`      | `_ci`        | `.ci/` |
| `myproject`| `_myproject` | `.myproject/` |

This means `--branch testing` and `--branch _testing` produce the same result.

### Examples

```bash
# Default: branch _agentrack, directory .agentrack/
agt init

# Custom branch for a dedicated test instance
agt init --branch testing
# Creates branch _testing, directory .testing/

# Multiple instances in one repo (each on its own branch)
agt init --branch frontend
agt init --branch backend
```

### Pointer file

After `agt init`, a pointer file (`.agentrack.json`) is created at the repository root. This file records the active branch name so that all subsequent commands (`push`, `pull`, etc.) know which worktree directory to use:

```json
{
  "branch": "_testing"
}
```

For backward compatibility, if `.agentrack.json` does not exist, commands assume the default branch (`_agentrack`) and directory (`.agentrack/`).

### Notes

- Must be run inside a git repository.
- Idempotent -- running it again won't overwrite existing data.
- Branch names cannot contain slashes (they would create nested directories). Use dashes instead: `--branch feature-test`.
- Handles two scenarios: creates a new orphan branch (fresh) or fetches an existing one (join). See [Storing issues in git](./storing-issues-in-git.md).
